thread:
mike: Quick summary / fyi — ran a tail-sensitivity sweep yesterday evening against kortex-v2 + kortex-v3 kernels using real-replay traces and our load harness. Observed p95 pretty stable but p99 spikes when microbatch_size >= 6 and KV-hit ratio drops below ~80%. Looks like batching convoy + cache cold starts.
anya: Can you paste the exact run command and which trace you replayed? Curious if this is synthetic mixing or pure customer trace.
mike: Used trace `prod-chat-2026-03-12.json` (5k sessions), harness run:
```
./bin/loadharness --mode replay --trace ./traces/prod-chat-2026-03-12.json \
  --concurrency 64 --microbatch-target 8 --observe p50,p95,p99 --kernel kortex-v2
```
kevin: Two quick notes: 1) Our replay tool recreates inter-arrival times but we don't rehydrate per-session KV prefetch by default — that underestimates warm-cache tail. 2) Synthetic burst tests (poisson + fixed prompt) show different convoying characteristics; you should compare both.
sara: This matches a perf regression we rolled two weeks ago (kernel switch + microbatch heuristics change). I dug into flamegraph for a p99 request — KV lookup latency jumped ~1.2x when the cache path took the fallback path. Trace snippet:
```
serving: trace_id=0x7f3a warm=false kernel=kortex-v2 batch=8 kv_hit=false queue_ms=74 exec_ms=325 total_ms=412
```
jordan: If kv_hit==false frequently at tail that's classic amplification: larger microbatches increase chance one cold request stalls the batch. For tail SLOs we should prefer smaller microbatches or adaptive microbatch that shrinks on queue depth.
anya: How are we reporting p95/p99? Are we including queuing time or only execution time? This matters a lot for comparing replay vs synthetic.
kevin: Currently dashboards show "response_time" = queue + exec + network. For kernel-level profiling we snapshot `exec_time` only. When people compare published kernel numbers (exec-only) to API SLO (response_time) they get confused.
perf-bot: Automated profile: kortex-v2@sha:abc123 — p50_exec=42ms p95_exec=120ms p99_exec=420ms sample_n=4820
mike: Action items proposed:
- Short term: run replay with `--kv-rehydrate` to approximate warm caches and compare p99 deltas. (kevin will run)
- Mid term: add microbatch adaptive policy: target 8 but drop to 2 when queue-time > 50ms (jordan + eng-runtime)
- Measurement: update dashboard to surface exec-only percentiles alongside response percentiles and tag runs as "replay:rehydrate" vs "replay:stateless" (anya + product)
- Investigate kernel regression: bisect kortex-v2 commits between v2.1.4 and v2.1.7 (sara + eng-ml)
kevin: Example rehydrate flag run:
```
./bin/loadharness --mode replay --trace ./traces/prod-chat-2026-03-12.json \
  --concurrency 64 --microbatch-target 8 --kv-rehydrate true --observe p50,p95,p99
```
sara: Also worth doing a small chaos experiment: randomly flip 0.5% of requests to cold-cache to see tail amplification under realistic hit rates.
jordan: Agree. Also recommend reporting p99.9 for exec-only in kernel benchmarks — it reveals kernel hot-path jitter even when p99 looks ok.
anya: One more caveat: synthetic Poisson tests under high concurrency underestimate queuing because they don't replicate session stickiness that creates bursts against same KV keys. Replay fixes that but needs rehydration to be fair.
mike: Good. Let's treat this thread as the central log for the runs. Kevin — can you push the `--kv-rehydrate` run results (summary table + raw CSV) by tomorrow morning? If p99_exec drops >20% with rehydrate, we'll prioritize adaptive microbatch + prefetch.
kevin: Will do. I'll attach CSV to this thread when done. :thumbsup:
sara: If we end up rolling a quick rollback for the kernel change we should plan a canary with exec-only and response-time SLO gates.
jordan: Also add a synthetic 'convoy' scenario to our standard perf suite: deterministic interleaving that forces microbatch filling behavior. That caught a similar issue in 2024.
mike: Awesome. Thanks all. I'll create a tiny RFC for the adaptive microbatch heuristic and link here.
